transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been feeling deeply depressed and sad for about a month now. But on top of that, for the past few months, I've been hearing and seeing things that other people can't, and it's really wearing me down.
Can you tell me more about when these depressive feelings and the hallucinations started, and did one seem to begin before the other?

The hallucinations started first, about four months ago, when I began hearing voices and seeing things that weren't there. The heavy feelings of sadness and losing interest in everything didn't set in until much later, about a month ago. So the things I was seeing and hearing definitely came first.
Aside from the hallucinations, have you experienced any unusual or distorted thoughts, such as delusions, or noticed any significant changes in your thinking patterns or behavior?

Yes, I have. Lately, I've felt like people are watching or monitoring me, and I keep thinking that completely random things on the street have some special, hidden meaning meant just for me. It's made me very anxious, so I've mostly been staying in my room and avoiding everyone.

For the period when you were experiencing hallucinations and delusions without the depressive symptoms, which was about three months, did these psychotic symptoms significantly impact your daily functioning and relationships?

I'm not quite sure how much those specific symptoms impacted my functioning during those first few months. I mostly just tried to get through each day, so I haven't really thought about how it affected my relationships or daily tasks back then.

Can you estimate how long the periods of depression have lasted in relation to the periods of psychotic symptoms, and have there been any periods where you've had no significant depressive or psychotic symptoms?

My overall struggles started about six months ago, with the hallucinations and delusions going on for about four months and the depression lasting just this past month. There was definitely a period of at least a few weeks where I had the voices and visions on their own without any depression. I haven't really had any time where I felt completely symptom-free since this all began.

During the periods where you only had psychotic symptoms without depression, were you still able to maintain your daily routines, work, or social relationships relatively normally, or were they significantly impaired?

Even before the depression started, I found it really hard to keep up with my daily routines because I had zero motivation to do anything. I also completely lost interest in talking to friends or family, so my social life was pretty much non-existent. It was definitely a struggle to function normally.

Did the emergence of depressive symptoms seem to have any effect on the intensity or frequency of your hallucinations and delusions, or did they seem to change in any way after the depression started?

I'm not really sure if the depression made the voices or visions any more intense. I haven't noticed a specific change in them, but dealing with both the hallucinations and the low mood at the same time lately has been really hard.
I'm sorry, I didn't quite catch what you said just now. Could you please repeat your question?
I'm sorry, I didn't catch what you just said. Could you please repeat that or let me know what you would like to ask?

Let's take a moment to review what we've discussed so far. I didn't have a chance to ask my next question, so let's start fresh. Can you tell me more about how you've been coping with both the hallucinations and the feelings of depression simultaneously?

Dealing with both the hallucinations and the heavy depression at the same time has been incredibly difficult. Honestly, I don't really know how I'm coping with it all right now. I just feel completely overwhelmed and exhausted.
